title: Speculum and bimanual pelvic examination
stem: Cubicle 4. A 26-year-old woman has lower abdominal pain and a vaginal discharge for 5 days. Her pregnancy test is negative. Perform a speculum and bimanual pelvic examination on the pelvic model, then present your findings.
notes:
Checked against the GMC guidance on intimate examinations and chaperones (2024), RCOG guidance on gynaecological examinations, and BASHH/NICE guidance on pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).

Intimate examination: explain why, what it involves and that she can stop at any time; obtain and record consent; offer a chaperone (and record their name, or her refusal); privacy to undress with a cover; gloves; warm and lubricate the speculum. Speculum: inspect the vulva first, insert the closed speculum along the vaginal axis (downward and backward), rotate and open to see the cervix; take swabs (endocervical NAAT for chlamydia and gonorrhoea; high vaginal swab); close before withdrawing. Bimanual: two fingers in the vagina, other hand on the abdomen; cervical motion tenderness, uterine size, position and tenderness, adnexal masses or tenderness.

PID (BASHH): treat on clinical suspicion (lower abdominal pain plus cervical motion or adnexal tenderness) without waiting for swabs: ceftriaxone 1 g IM once plus doxycycline 100 mg twice daily and metronidazole 400 mg twice daily for 14 days (outpatient regimen). Admit if severely unwell, pregnant, or tubo-ovarian abscess.

Your notes list 'Bimanual pelvic exam' and 'PV exam' without detail; nothing conflicts.

turns.line: The nurse said you need to do an internal examination?

opts.t: Yes — I'd like to look at the neck of the womb with a speculum and then feel with two fingers, to find the cause of the pain. It may be uncomfortable; you can ask me to stop at any time. Is that OK?
opts.mark: Explains the examination and obtains consent

opts.t: Just lie back, it'll be quick.
opts.r: Wait, what are you going to do?

turns.line: Does someone else have to be here?

opts.t: I'd like a chaperone, Nurse Chaperone, to be present; I'll note her name. I'll leave while you undress and there's a sheet to cover you.
opts.mark: Offers a chaperone and ensures privacy

opts.t: No, we don't bother with that.
opts.r: I'd feel better with someone here…

steps.label: Examine
steps.hint: Abdomen first, vulva, speculum and swabs, then bimanual.

Prepare.t: Wash hands, gloves, warm and lubricate the speculum; position (knees bent, ankles together, knees apart)

Prepare.r: Tender in both iliac fossae, no guarding.

Speculum.r: Normal vulva, some yellow discharge at the introitus.

Speculum.t: Insert the closed speculum, rotate, open, visualise the cervix
Speculum.r: Cervix inflamed, bleeds on contact, mucopurulent discharge from the os.

Speculum.t: Swabs: endocervical NAAT (chlamydia/gonorrhoea) and high vaginal swab

Speculum.r: Closed as it comes out past the cervix.

Bimanual.t: Move the cervix gently side to side

Bimanual.r: Tender on both sides, no mass.

opts.t: Mucopurulent cervicitis, cervical motion and bilateral adnexal tenderness, negative pregnancy test: pelvic inflammatory disease
opts.mark: Presents findings and a working diagnosis of PID

opts.t: Start treatment now without waiting for swabs: ceftriaxone 1 g IM, doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days; partner notification; review in 72 hours
opts.mark: Treats empirically with BASHH regimen and arranges follow-up

opts.t: Wait for the swab results before any antibiotics
opts.r: Delayed treatment increases the risk of infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

qs.q: Minimum criteria to treat PID empirically?
qs.a: Lower abdominal pain with cervical motion or adnexal tenderness
Infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain
